opportunities.title: Where Is “Enough”? AI and the Missing Sense of Proportion
opportunities.text: Where Is “Enough”? AI and the Missing Sense of Proportion # Where Is “Enough”? AI and the Missing Sense of Proportion There is something I keep noticing when I work with AI. It is not simply a problem of accuracy. It is a problem of proportion. AI often seems to have difficulty finding the middle between: > “This requires maximum seriousness, control, precision, and verification.” and: > “This is probably fine. Let’s move on.” The boundary between those two states is strangely unstable. Humans are not perfect at this either. We overreact, underreact, obsess over irrelevant things, ignore important ones, spend three days fixing something that did not matter, and sometimes walk past a problem that later becomes enormous. opportunities.title: Robotics safety cannot be a prompt engineering problem
opportunities.text: Robotics safety cannot be a prompt engineering problem We are teaching machines to fly by asking them to be polite. The industry is currently treating physical safety as a linguistic alignment problem. We assume that if we can nudge a model to refuse a harmful command through chain-of-thought prompting or better in-context learning, the physical world will follow suit. It will not. A recent study, "Defining and Evaluating Physical Safety for Large Language Models," highlights a structural mismatch that prompt engineering cannot bridge. The researchers developed an LLM drone safety benchmark that classifies risks into human-targeted threats, object-targeted threats, infrastructure attacks, and regulatory violations.
